findings.reason: a §2 node starting from "stop only targets the pid" hunts the wrong mechanism, where the plan's own evidence points at why a group signal failed to reach a reparented worker.
findings.text: §1 states the orphan survived because `crew stop` "targets only the recorded pid", but the cited path signals the whole process group: `terminate` (dispatch_sessions.py:1752) calls `_signal_process_group` (routing.py:2915), whose docstring reads "os.killpg signals the whole process group". §1 itself then notes the group stop "should end it", so the sentence asserts a cause the plan's own citation contradicts, and §2's candidate list (worker record absent / pid changed by reparenting / classifier bypass) never covers the group-signal path that is the actual open question

findings.reason: a node that establishes the gap in `local_liveness` is fenced out of the only file that can close it, so the plan must add recovery_liveness.py to the write paths or drop that candidate from the list.
findings.text: §2's deliverable leaves the classification repair open among three named sites ("in `local_liveness`, in the worker record's writer, or in the classifier's call") but the declared write paths are routing.py, dispatch_launch.py, dispatch_sessions.py, recovery_classification.py and the new test file, so the `local_liveness` site — which lives in `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py` — is outside the node's fence. Verified: `local_liveness` is defined at recovery_liveness.py:730 and recovery_classification.py:149 calls it, and recovery_liveness.py is in no live claim and no other section's write paths

findings.reason: a provenance date on background files; the three tests exist and the guards they name are real, so the measure is unaffected.
findings.text: §3 says "Three test files, landed 2026-10-03" lock the guards in, but `git log --diff-filter=A` shows test_resume_refuses_a_live_worker.py added 2026-10-03 while test_resume_sweep_needs_an_observed_death.py and test_direct_resume_needs_an_observed_death.py were added 2026-09-29

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §3 dates three cited test files to a single landing day that two of them do not have.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2's done-when names four measurable cases (real processes in a temp tree, checked by pid afterwards) with a declared negative control that signals the supervisor pid alone and fails the first case; §3's names four cases with a declared control that restores the reproduced cause and fails the reproduced case.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both negative controls are "logged under the run directory" (the durable crew run dir, not a scratchpad) and reproduction findings are recorded in the manifest, a persisted path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the plan proposes extending `signal_worker` and names no new symbol by plan label, ticket number or version tag; `s1`/`s2`/`s3`, the gate id and the cross-plan `crew-runtime-positive-controls §47` reference are plan-structure data, not code.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — §1's stated cause is refuted by the code it cites, and §2's open repair-site list exceeds its declared write paths.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one invariant (a worker never outlives its supervisor) and §3 one (a resume never launches beside a live attempt); §2's three repair bullets enforce the same invariant at termination and classification layers and close on one gate.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the one depends-on (`s3 → a-run-has-one-live-writer#s2`) resolves to a section that exists, the single gate `g-arholw-routing-released` gates `s2` and names the in-flight run that holds `reckon/crew/routing.py`, and a live-claim scan of the files §2/§3 write shows routing.py is the only claimed path and it is the one gated.
